name: Torta Negra
desc: Black cake: the dark, rich fruit cake of the Welsh in Patagonia, made to keep through a winter and a long journey. Teisen ddu, the old recipe says. Restores 160 HP.

name: Cordero Patagónico
desc: Patagonian lamb, slow roasted over an open fire on an iron cross, the way the gauchos do it. It takes all afternoon. Restores 200 HP.

name: Mate Gourd
desc: A hollowed gourd and a metal straw, the bombilla, for mate, the bitter herb tea Argentines pass round a circle. Welsh Patagonians drink it in the morning and tea in the afternoon.

name: Gaiman Shawl
desc: A woollen shawl woven in the Chubut valley, warm enough for a wind that has come all the way from the Andes.
msg: {name} held fast in the Gaiman Shawl!

name: Maple Syrup
desc: A tin of Canadian maple syrup, tapped from sugar maples in spring and boiled down: about forty litres of sap for one of syrup. Restores 120 HP.

name: Cape Breton Oatcakes
desc: Thick, crumbly oatcakes, a little sweeter than the Scottish kind, from a recipe that came over with the Gaels. Restores 100 HP.

name: Lobster Roll
desc: Fresh lobster in a buttered bun, a summer treat all along the coast of Atlantic Canada. Restores 190 HP.

name: Milled Tweed
desc: A length of tweed thickened at a milling frolic, thumped on a table to the beat of Gaelic songs. Warm as a ceilidh.
msg: {name} was kept warm by the Milled Tweed!

name: Clam Chowder
desc: New England clam chowder: clams, potatoes, onion and cream, thick enough to stand a spoon in. Boston says Manhattan's red version isn't chowder. Restores 160 HP.

name: Irish Soda Bread
desc: Soda bread from a Boston bakery, made the way Irish grandmothers made it, with buttermilk and a cross cut on top. Restores 100 HP.

name: Boston Cream Pie
desc: Which is a cake, not a pie: sponge, custard and chocolate on top. Massachusetts made it the state dessert in 1996. Restores 140 HP.

name: Emigrant's Claddagh
desc: A claddagh ring, two hands holding a crowned heart, carried from Ireland by an emigrant and handed down. Love, loyalty and friendship.
msg: {name} was steadied by the Emigrant's Claddagh!

name: Biscuits and Gravy
desc: Southern biscuits, which are soft scone-like rolls, under a thick white sausage gravy. Breakfast in the mountains. Restores 140 HP.

name: Cornbread
desc: A wedge of cornbread from a cast-iron skillet. Maize was a Native American crop that every settler family learnt to grow. Restores 100 HP.

name: Sweet Tea
desc: Iced tea with a great deal of sugar in it, the house drink of the American South. A British visitor's soul leaves their body. Restores 80 HP.

name: Dulcimer Pick
desc: A goose-quill pick for a mountain dulcimer, the zither the Appalachian settlers made for themselves.
msg: {name} kept time with the Dulcimer Pick!

name: Roscoff Onions
desc: Pink onions from Roscoff, sweet and long-keeping, the ones the Onion Johnnies sold door to door in Britain. Roasted, they restore 100 HP.

name: Kouign-Amann
desc: Butter cake from Douarnenez: bread dough folded with butter and sugar until it caramelises. Kouign is cake and amann is butter. Restores 150 HP.

name: Breton Cider
desc: Dry Breton cider, served in a bowl. Yec'hed mat: good health. Restores 120 HP.

name: String of Onions
desc: A string of pink Roscoff onions, plaited by the stalks, the way the Onion Johnnies carried them to Britain. For somebody in Plymouth.

name: Triskell Pin
desc: A pin with the triskell, three spirals joined in the middle, an old Celtic pattern that Bretons wear as a sign of Brittany.
msg: {name} was guarded by the Triskell Pin!

name: Well-Stamped Passport
desc: Your passport, stamped in Trelew, Sydney (Nova Scotia), Boston, Tri-Cities and Roscoff, and signed in the back by a bard, an archdruid, a councillor, a fiddler and a storyteller. The kin of these isles abroad count you as one of their own.
